title: Noether applied
lede: Where is a number that never changes used today? The same move four times, sorted by what stays: two ways of stepping a planet for a billion steps, a network told about energy, a loop of stirred air, a protein chain that turns with its input. Part 2 of 3.

chapters.title: Networks, air and a chain, sorted by what stays
What must never change in your system?

captions: Last time: a number that never changes.
Where is that used today, outside quantum physics?
First: a computer moves a planet in tiny steps.
Each dot is a snapshot of that planet.
1,000 snapshots from each of two ways of stepping.
1,000,000,000 tiny steps each.
From above: two rings round the sun.
Now sort by the number that should stay.
One stays on its shell. The other leaves.
The energy-keeper never strays more than 0.007 %.
The plain way: 1.9 % off after 10,000,000 steps.
About 270 times more error.
Then it is thrown out: by 65 million steps.
The spin number stays right to 11 places.
Astronomers run whole solar systems this way.
Next: machines that learn. Each dot is one step.
10,000 steps from 100 training runs.
Sort by the gap between two layers.
The weights travelled 0.24.
The gap between layers moved 0.00095.
Teach two networks a swinging spring.
Same size: 200 units, 2,000 training steps.
The plain network, energy error: 170.
The energy-keeping network: 0.38.
About 450 times lower.
Weather: tag a loop of air and follow it.
The loop stretches and folds.
The swirl around it stays the same.
One dot per residue: 2,180 in one chain.
Turn the protein. The answer turns with it.
What stays is its shape, not a saved number.
Monday: what must never change in your system?

brand.takeaway: Find what stays. Then build so it does.

sources: S1
NASA NSSDC Earth fact sheet: eccentricity 0.0167 (the shape of both steppers' orbit). https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/earthfact.html
S2
topic folder verlet_vs_rk4.c + data/trace.c + recompute.py (gcc, seed 20261010): velocity Verlet vs classical RK4, 100 steps per lap, 1,000,000,000 steps. Derived.
S3
Wisdom and Holman, Astron. J. 102, 1528 (1991); Hairer, Lubich, Wanner, Acta Numerica 2003; Laskar and Gastineau, Nature 459, 817 (2009).
S4
Large or variable steps break the symplectic guarantee: arXiv 2111.08835 (honest line).
S5
Greydanus, Dzamba, Yosinski, Hamiltonian Neural Networks, NeurIPS 2019, arXiv 1906.01563, Table 1: 170 vs 0.38 (units 1e-3).
S6
Du, Hu, Lee, Algorithmic regularization in learning deep homogeneous models, NeurIPS 2018, arXiv 1806.00900.
S7
Kunin et al., Neural mechanics, ICLR 2021, arXiv 2012.04728: finite learning rates break the conservation (honest line).
S8
Part 1 (noether-symmetry) recompute v2, seed 20261010: 100 runs x 100 steps, weights travel 0.2378, the sum 0.000952. MODEL.
S9
Kelvin 1869; Salmon, Annu. Rev. Fluid Mech. 20 (1988); the loop is our own point-vortex model (recompute.py C). MODEL.
Jumper et al., Nature 596, 583 (2021), Fig. 1d: CASP14 target T1044, 2,180 residues. The chain drawn is a seeded stand-in, not the fold.
honest: Pictures are simulated. Big steps break it. A turn saves no number.
